column1: # v21 against v19: does the integer-throughput result scale, or was v19 a one-off?
# v19 moved the `;` compare to the vector unit and won 23 ms at 18 threads against an
# instruction-count prediction of 1.5. v20 is its control — 9.5 instructions a row *smaller* and
# 16 ms slower. The model that fits both is that this loop is bound on integer ALU throughput
# specifically, and that the vector unit beside it is idle.
# That model has one calibration point and it is v19's own arm. This batch is the test of whether
# it is a rate or a coincidence.
# v21 moves the rest of the scan's byte-lane work the same way: `keep = (1 << (tz & 0x38)) - 1`
# and `w & keep` become a `cmhi` against `[0, 1, .. 15]` and one `and.16b`, which also makes both
# `csel` for klo/khi unnecessary, and the delimiter index comes off one `shrn` extract instead of
# two extracts, an `orr`, a `cbz` and a `csel`. The hash is untouched and bit-identical.
# Counted with scripts/loopcount.py before the batch, integer = total - loads - stores - branches
# - vector - transfers:
#                 insns/row   integer/row   measured vs v12
# So v21 is -16.5 integer ops a row against v19's -6.5. Straight-lining v19's own rate gives
# -58 ms, which nobody should believe: the loop still issues 13 loads a row and still waits on a
# dependent table load, and one of those has to become the bound before the integer side runs out.
# The honest prediction is a wide -20 to -55.
# What each outcome means. Near -50: the rate is real, the model generalises, and the remaining
# integer work in the *parser* is the next target on the same argument. Near -20: there is a rate
# but it is sublinear, and the batch after this one should find the new bound rather than move
# more work. Near zero: v19 was not a rate at all and its 23 ms needs a different explanation,
# because this change is strictly more of the same thing.
# REPS=7, matching the v20 batch. v19 and v21 are each entered twice under two labels at 18
# threads; those two spreads are the batch's noise floor and nothing smaller may be read.
v19 t18 (dup)
v21 t18 (dup)
v12 t8
v19 t8
v21 t8
